newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Kabul bombed for second night.
newsitem.headline: Kabul bombed for second night.

text.p: Anti-Taleban forces bombed Kabul for the second night running on Sunday, sending another big barrage of anti-aircraft fire blazing into the night.
The first two explosions, accompanied by outgoing fire from the purist Islamic defenders of the Afghan capital, occurred around 11 p.m. (1830 GMT). They were followed a few minutes later by a third.
The bombs landed two hours after curfew and it was not immediately clear what they had struck.

Warplanes, identified by the Taleban as belonging to northern Uzbek leader Abdul Rashid Dostum whose forces have been fighting on plains north of Kabul, bombed the capital twice on Saturday night and again on Sunday morning.

They were apparently aiming for the airport on the northeast edge of the city, but one landed in a city centre park. There were no reports of casualties or serious damage and the Taleban said the bombers missed the airport.
